name: Action outbox
what: Every external side effect, durably recorded before it happens, with reconciliation state.
reason: The live reconciliation registry is not attached to this publisher.

name: Autonomy queue
what: What VESPER intends to do unprompted, before it does it.
reason: The live autonomy loop is not attached to this publisher.

name: Emergency stop
what: Halt everything. Independent of the thing it stops, by design.
reason: The native bridge exposes no independent stop command. In the existing app, hold Globe/Fn + Control + Option + Command for 0.6 seconds to stop VESPER; Globe three times starts it again. This panel cannot invoke that native stop.

name: Grants
what: Standing permissions, their scope, and their expiry.
reason: The running policy decision point is not attached to this publisher.

name: Verification state
what: What's been verified, what's asserted, and the refusal to let repetition count as success.
reason: The live verifier is not attached to this publisher.

name: Follow-me
what: The interface moving with VESPER as it relocates.
reason: No relocation-to-interface transport is registered on this surface.

name: Grant templates
what: Reusable permission sets — 'study mode', 'travel mode', 'hands off'.
reason: No owner-defined grant template collection or governed apply operation exists.

name: Hardware access
what: Camera, microphone, screen, files — what's granted, what's in use, and a capture indicator that can't lie.
reason: The native bridge publishes neither active capture sessions nor complete permission state. Device presence is not access consent.

name: Import / export
what: Take your memory with you, or seed it from somewhere else.
reason: No portable memory transfer operation is exposed by the native bridge. Copying live database files would lose WAL records.

name: Live activity stream
what: A running narration of what VESPER is doing, at a granularity you set.
reason: No runtime event stream has been supplied to this publisher.

name: Modes
what: Study / travel / low-power / hands-off — whole configurations you switch between.
reason: The existing permission mode does not define study, travel, low-power, or hands-off configurations. Those presets need governed definitions before they can be applied.

name: Panic revoke
what: Drop every standing grant at once, without stopping VESPER.
reason: The policy decision point has no public revoke-all operation, and the native bridge has no revoke command.

name: Per-app rules
what: What VESPER may touch in each application, separately.
reason: No per-application policy collection or governed editor exists.

name: Quiet-hours restrictions
what: Narrower permissions at night than during the day.
reason: No owner-defined quiet-hours authorization policy exists. Alarm overrides must remain intact.

name: Remote surfaces
what: Reaching VESPER from a phone or another machine.
reason: No enrolled endpoint inventory is attached to this publisher.

name: Work rate
what: Throughput over time — is VESPER actually getting things done.
reason: No bounded runtime completion history has been supplied.

name: macOS permissions
what: Accessibility, Screen Recording, Automation — what's granted, what's needed for which feature, and why.
reason: Permission status is not exported by the native bridge. Querying permissions from a helper would report the helper’s identity, not the app’s.

name: Attestation state
what: Whether a VESPER-controlled segment exists and is attested. Today: false, so no node is a full host.
reason: The network fabric contract could not be read.

name: Battery health
what: Capacity, cycles, temperature history, daily charge range. The numbers that decide the ten-year question.
reason: No usable battery capacity and cycle counters were returned.

name: Capability registry
what: Every capability, its level, and the constants that are refused outright.
reason: The running capability registry is not attached to this publisher.

name: Charge policy
what: Charge limit state, and whether the machine is sitting at high charge — the mechanism that aged this pack to 84% in a shop.
reason: The OS did not return battery charge range or charge-limit state.

name: Compensation
what: What each in-flight action would undo if it fails partway.
reason: The running executor’s compensator registry is not attached to this publisher.

name: Compressor & swap
what: How hard the compressor is working, and whether swap has turned on. Swap is the SSD-wear tripwire.
reason: The OS did not return compressor and swap counters.

name: Control-plane lease
what: Which node holds control, its fencing token, and its refusal to self-promote.
reason: No readable leased-domain state was supplied.

name: Degradation ladder
what: What VESPER gives up first when it must give something up.
reason: The governed degradation contract could not be read.

name: Endpoints
what: Every surface VESPER can reach you through, as profiles rather than device names.
reason: The live device registry is not attached to this publisher.

name: Enrollment
what: Admit a new machine, measure it, and watch it earn placement on merit.
reason: No live enrollment registry is instantiated by this runtime. Discovery and admission cannot be performed by the display.

name: Governed surfaces
what: Which files require review, and who reviews them.
reason: The governed-surface artifact could not be read.

name: Key & identity state
what: Each node's keys, where they're stored, and which never leave the device.
reason: No enrolled device key-storage profiles were supplied. Key material is never read by this panel.

name: Memory headroom
what: Real reclaimable memory, translated — not the alarming 'free' figure that reads 0.16 GB on a healthy machine.
reason: The host adapter could not read reclaimable memory.

name: Memory pressure band
what: The kernel's own signal, shown as a band. Never converted to gigabytes — it doesn't track allocation.
reason: The kernel did not expose a pressure band.

name: Network segments
what: Private / shared / outside, each with its trust ceiling. No addresses, no product names.
reason: The declared network segments could not be read.

name: Node profiles
what: What each machine measurably sustains. UNKNOWN means unavailable, and shows as such.
reason: No live enrolled measured profiles were supplied.

name: Owner working set
what: What's resident right now, so a headroom number is interpretable rather than just a figure.
reason: The OS process resident-memory inventory was unavailable.

name: Placement decisions
what: Where each capability currently runs and why it was placed there, including what lost.
reason: No live placement assignment or decision history was supplied.

name: Platform adapters
what: Per-platform translation of host signals. The knowledge lives in the adapter, never in shared logic.
reason: The host adapter could not be loaded.

name: Survival profile
what: What VESPER carries onto the last device standing, and what it drops.
reason: No enrolled placement profile with measured resource budgets was supplied.

name: Trust zones
what: Z0–Z3 per node, with the reason each landed where it did.
reason: No enrolled effective trust assignments were supplied. A key-storage ceiling alone is not an effective trust zone.

name: Before/after
what: Measure a change you made and show whether it actually helped.
reason: Capture a fresh baseline and a later reading in this panel to compare them.

name: Command palette
what: Keyboard-first access to every surface in this document.
reason: The palette is available locally through the instruments panel or Command-K.

name: Costing me now
what: Live ranked list of what is draining the battery this minute.
reason: Public process CPU and RSS counters do not measure battery energy. Per-process power attribution requires privileged powermetrics.

name: Disk I/O rate
what: Live read/write throughput, and cumulative writes against SSD endurance.
reason: Two comparable storage-counter samples are needed before a rate can be measured.

name: Display power
what: Brightness and its real cost. The display dominates idle drain, so this is a bigger lever than CPU.
reason: The public display inventory does not report measured display watts. Brightness alone cannot establish power cost.

name: Link quality
what: Latency, throughput and reliability per path — measured at enrollment, never declared.
reason: No enrollment-measured per-path latency, throughput, and reliability record is published. A TCP reachability check is not that measurement.

name: Maintenance actions
what: Things worth doing occasionally, surfaced when they're due rather than remembered.
reason: No maintenance schedule or last-completed action ledger has been configured.

name: Node roles
what: What each machine is FOR — always-on server, travelling laptop, phone endpoint.
reason: The live enrollment registry has not published role assignments. Availability classes are not roles.

name: Peripherals
what: What's plugged in, what it draws, and what it keeps awake.
reason: No public peripheral inventory was returned.

name: Radio state
what: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth power cost, and what's keeping them awake.
reason: No public radio-state observation was returned.

name: Relocation history
what: When VESPER moved, what triggered it, and the damping that stopped it flapping.
reason: No placement events are available in the supplied bounded log tail.

name: Retry policy
what: What VESPER does when something fails, per task class.
reason: The running reconciler’s retry policy could not be read.

name: Sleep & wake log
what: Every sleep, wake, and what woke it. Where mystery battery drain gets explained.
reason: The public power-management log could not be read.

name: Storage & SSD
what: Free space, TRIM, SMART, and cumulative write pressure.
reason: The public disk inventory could not be read.

name: Thermal history
what: Temperature over time against ambient — the variable that matters most in site B heat.
reason: No battery-temperature samples have been collected. Ambient temperature is unavailable.

name: Throttle events
what: When the machine actually throttled, and what was running.
reason: The public power-management interface returned no recorded performance-warning status.

name: Approval history
what: Everything you've ever approved, and the chance to withdraw any of it.
reason: No approval records are available in the supplied bounded audit tail. Withdrawal is unavailable without a revoke operation.

name: Blast radius
what: What breaks if a given node dies — simulated before it happens.
reason: No enrolled placement profiles and assignments were supplied for simulation.

name: Clock skew
what: How far apart the nodes' clocks are — and the reminder that HLC, not wall clock, decides order.
reason: No bounded request/response clock observations from other nodes were supplied. Local timestamps alone cannot establish skew.

name: Migration dry-run
what: Move VESPER somewhere, in simulation, and see what degrades.
reason: No enrolled placement profiles were supplied for simulation.

name: Node comparison
what: Two machines side by side on every measured axis.
reason: At least two enrolled measured node profiles are needed for comparison.

name: Onboarding wizard
what: Walk a new machine from nothing to enrolled and measured.
reason: The native bridge has no discovery, measurement, or admission command. The wizard can prepare a request but cannot enroll a node.

name: Ambient estimate
what: Inferred room temperature — the ceiling the battery can never get below.
reason: There is no ambient-temperature sensor. Battery temperature is not room temperature.

name: Behaviour on / off this Mac
what: Different rules when VESPER is here versus running on another node.
reason: The owner has not defined the location-dependent policy. No policy is inferred.

name: Charging schedule
what: When to charge, given your day, to minimise time at high state of charge.
reason: The owner has not supplied a charging schedule, and no governed charging-control action is available.

name: Consent channel policy
what: Which tiers may be approved by voice and which need a tap you make yourself.
reason: The owner has not decided which approval tiers may use voice versus an explicit tap.

name: Failover drill
what: Deliberately kill a node and prove recovery works. A negative control for the fabric.
reason: This action deliberately kills a node. Separate explicit owner authorization is required; icon approval does not authorize a drill.

name: Fan & acoustics
what: Fan speed and noise — heat you can hear before you can measure it.
reason: No supported public fan-speed or acoustic-power sensor is exposed to this publisher.

name: Power draw
what: Whole-machine watts split into compute vs everything else. Compute is 8% at idle — the split is the insight.
reason: Whole-machine compute-versus-other power attribution requires privileged powermetrics. No root-access workaround is attempted.

name: Process energy
what: Per-process power attribution — who is actually costing you battery, ranked.
reason: Per-process power attribution requires privileged powermetrics tasks. CPU usage is not watts.
